correctness.rationale: The hub-free subcomplex is A=∗ᵢ Ind(P_{mᵢ−2}); at most one spoke can be chosen, and each spoke attaches a cone on the join with only that petal's factor shortened by one endpoint. To see the path recurrence, for a path on n≥3 vertices send vertex n−2 to n, fixing the other vertices. This gives a simplicial retraction on independence complexes contiguous to the identity, since N(n)⊆N(n−2); deleting n−2 leaves P_{n−3} and an edge. The recurrence and the n=0,1,2 bases give the three residue types. In the 2-residue case the shortened factor includes by a homotopy equivalence: the added endpoint has contractible link Ind(P_{3k−2}). With at least two 0-residue petals the base and every spoke link are contractible. With one such petal, the base is contractible, and its two spokes have spherical links S^{K−2}; their maps factor through the contractible base even after the first attachment. With no 0-residue petals the base is S^{K−1}; 1-residue links are contractible. If there are any 2-residue spokes, the first kills the base and the other 2ν₂−1 have null-homotopic attaching maps and add its suspensions. All attachments are along subcomplexes. For triangular petals the shortened factor is the augmented join unit; r≥2 ensures an exceptional spherical link is nonempty. Since K≥2, the noncontractible cases have positive reduced homology in the specified degree. Line 10's u₀ is a notation typo for ν₀, whose meaning is unambiguous from the definition and proof.
residual_risks: The 48 output cases are not all two- or three-petal bouquets: verify.py lines 81–84 also include the six one-cycle tests (42 in-scope cases). This wording error does not affect the homotopy proof. Finite-field checks do not prove contractibility or exclude all torsion.

value.rationale: Vertex-gluing cycles of arbitrary lengths is a natural family where the broad outerplanar theorem leaves all numerical invariants undetermined. The mixed theorem identifies a new contractibility boundary through the number of 0-residue petals, and determines the dimension and multiplicity in every other residue pattern, rather than just giving another equal-petal count. The endpoint-inclusion analysis explains the distinction between killing a sphere and adding suspensions.
residual_risks: The classification is nonequivariant and does not address arbitrary block/cut-vertex gluing.
